condition: Perianal abscess with cellulitis in poorly controlled diabetes
summary: 58-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, five days of perianal pain, 6 cm of surrounding cellulitis, T 38.4, HR 104, glucose 19. Drain today and give antibiotics; glycaemic control; examine for necrotising infection.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful swelling beside the back passage with fever
inputs.hpi: Five days of worsening pain and swelling to the left of the anus, now spreading redness onto the buttock, fevers and sweats. Type 2 diabetes on metformin and gliclazide, sugars 15–20 at home this week. No pain out of proportion, no skin discolouration, no crackling under the skin.

exam.other: Perianal: 5 cm fluctuant tender left ischioanal swelling with 6 cm of surrounding erythema onto the buttock; no crepitus, no skin necrosis, no scrotal involvement.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Ischioanal abscess with cellulitis, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Left ischioanal abscess with surrounding cellulitis and systemic features in poorly controlled diabetes. Drainage under GA today, IV antibiotics, glycaemic control; low threshold for necrotising infection.

mustNotMiss.note: Diabetes + perianal sepsis with cellulitis: necrotising infection must be considered.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano and rectovaginal fistula
guideline.section: Antibiotics after drainage for surrounding cellulitis, systemic infection, diabetes/immunosuppression
guideline.citation: Gaertner WB, Burgess PL, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, and rectovaginal fistula. Dis Colon Rectum. 2022;65:964–985.

guideline.name: WSES/SIS-E consensus — management of skin and soft-tissue infections (incl. necrotising soft-tissue infection, Fournier’s gangrene)
guideline.section: Necrotising soft-tissue infection: suspect in diabetics with perineal infection; early surgical exploration
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Guirao X, Hardcastle TC, et al. 2018 WSES/SIS-E consensus conference: recommendations for the management of skin and soft-tissue infections. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:58.

rationale: Permutation: diabetes, cellulitis and SIRS. Antibiotics become indicated; necrotising infection moves onto the differential.
